propositions.question: Which Lovable Build mode runtime is identified?
propositions.status: Current name and dated milestones; runtime unresolved
propositions.answer: Current publisher documentation names Build mode and identifies Agent mode as its former name; the dated Agent-mode transition and model milestone do not identify the current service revision.
propositions.whyItMatters: A publisher-sourced rename and hosted milestones do not freeze the runtime behind a later task.

propositions.question: Which model executes a task?
propositions.answer: A dated changelog entry names an incorporated model, but current routing and endpoint identity remain unknown.
propositions.whyItMatters: Service identity and model identity change on different schedules.

propositions.question: What does Build mode change?
propositions.answer: Current docs distinguish non-writing Plan mode from Build mode that applies multi-file changes and exposes diffs and summaries.
propositions.whyItMatters: The active mode determines file authority.

propositions.question: Where can work run in parallel?
propositions.status: Serial main queue; conditional parallel read-only subagents
propositions.answer: The main Build-mode prompt queue processes one task at a time, while temporary read-only subagents may perform separate investigations in parallel and report findings to the main agent.
propositions.whyItMatters: Parallel read-only investigation is not parallel project-writing authority.

propositions.question: Which checks may run?
propositions.answer: Browser, frontend and edge checks are documented, with many paths requiring an explicit request or confirmation.
propositions.whyItMatters: Tool availability does not prove any check ran.

propositions.question: Which backend actions and region apply?
propositions.answer: Cloud tools can be always allowed, asked each time or denied, and new projects can use several regions.
propositions.whyItMatters: Backend mutation authority and execution location are separately configurable.

propositions.question: Where do changes go?
propositions.status: GitHub sync and publish are separate
propositions.answer: A connected GitHub App can sync the linked repository, while a live deployment requires an explicit Publish or Update action.
propositions.whyItMatters: Repository mutation does not automatically imply live deployment.

propositions.question: Was this service independently evaluated here?
propositions.answer: No reproducible exact-service evaluation passed into this dossier.
propositions.whyItMatters: Publisher documentation is attribution, not observed behavior.
